pack.description: Academic collocations: word partnerships that make written and spoken arguments sound natural.
pack.selection_note: Internal high-yield selection of word combinations that recur in academic writing and discussion; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: to be one of the things that cause or influence a result
entries.example_academic: Diet plays a role in the development of the disease, but genes matter more.
entries.example_spoken: Luck played a role, but she also worked really hard.

entries.definition: to decide that something is true after thinking about the facts
entries.example_academic: It is too early to draw a conclusion from a single season of data.
entries.example_spoken: Don't draw a conclusion before you've read the whole article.

entries.definition: to carry out a careful study in order to discover new facts
entries.example_academic: The team conducted research on sleep patterns among shift workers.
entries.example_spoken: She's conducting research on bees for her thesis.

entries.definition: to make more people know about a problem or subject
entries.example_academic: The campaign raised awareness of the risks of antibiotic overuse.
entries.example_spoken: We're selling coffee to raise awareness about food waste.

entries.definition: to be something that could cause harm or danger
entries.example_academic: Rising sea levels pose a threat to coastal cities.
entries.example_spoken: Does the construction pose a threat to the old trees?

entries.definition: to produce a strong effect on someone or something
entries.example_academic: Early childhood education has an impact on earnings decades later.
entries.example_spoken: The new schedule had a big impact on my sleep.

entries.definition: to consider something when you are judging a situation or making a decision
entries.example_academic: The estimate does not take into account the cost of maintenance.
entries.example_spoken: You have to take the commute into account when you choose an apartment.

entries.definition: to recognize or point out that two things are different
entries.example_academic: The author makes a distinction between income and wealth.
entries.example_spoken: We need to make a distinction between urgent and important tasks.

entries.definition: to collect facts or numbers for a study
entries.example_academic: Researchers gathered data from more than two hundred schools.
entries.example_spoken: We're gathering data for our survey in the cafeteria.

entries.definition: to watch, listen to or think about something carefully
entries.example_academic: Earlier studies paid little attention to the role of women in the trade.
entries.example_spoken: Pay attention to the dates; they'll be on the test.

entries.definition: a large number of different things of the same general kind
entries.example_academic: The enzyme is active across a wide range of temperatures.
entries.example_spoken: The gym offers a wide range of classes.

entries.definition: to move forward in your work or toward a goal
entries.example_academic: Researchers have made progress toward a vaccine in recent years.
entries.example_spoken: I finally made progress on my essay last night.

entries.definition: to get knowledge or skill by doing something over time
entries.example_academic: Graduates gain experience through placements in local firms.
entries.example_spoken: I want to gain experience before I apply for a master's.

entries.definition: to do or have what a rule or standard demands
entries.example_academic: Buildings constructed before the reform do not meet the requirements for fire safety.
entries.example_spoken: Does this course meet the requirement for my major?

entries.definition: to cause people to think about or discuss a matter
entries.example_academic: The findings raise a question about the reliability of earlier surveys.
entries.example_spoken: That raises a question: who's going to pay for it?

entries.definition: to give facts that show something is true
entries.example_academic: The fossils provide evidence of a much warmer climate.
entries.example_spoken: Can you provide evidence that you were sick?

entries.definition: to use an opportunity or situation to get a benefit
entries.example_academic: Firms took advantage of low interest rates to expand.
entries.example_spoken: You should take advantage of the free tutoring.

entries.definition: to try hard to do something
entries.example_academic: The government made an effort to consult rural communities.
entries.example_spoken: He made an effort to arrive on time this week.

entries.definition: over a period of time that continues far into the future
entries.example_academic: In the long term, investment in education raises national income.
entries.example_spoken: In the long term, it's cheaper to buy a bike than to take the bus.

entries.definition: to talk formally to a group of people about a subject
entries.example_academic: Each student gives a presentation on a published article.
entries.example_spoken: I have to give a presentation in my seminar tomorrow.

entries.definition: to choose what to do after thinking about it
entries.example_academic: The committee will make a decision once all the reports have been received.
entries.example_spoken: I need to make a decision about housing by Friday.

entries.definition: more and more of a particular kind of person or thing
entries.example_academic: A growing number of studies link air quality to school performance.
entries.example_spoken: A growing number of students are taking classes online.

entries.definition: to accept that you are the person who must deal with something or who caused it
entries.example_academic: Local councils took responsibility for maintaining the roads.
entries.example_spoken: Someone has to take responsibility for booking the room.

entries.definition: to decide what you want to achieve
entries.example_academic: The agreement set a goal of halving emissions within twenty years.
entries.example_spoken: I set a goal of reading one article a day.

entries.definition: to finish something by the time it is due
entries.example_academic: Contractors who fail to meet a deadline pay a daily penalty.
entries.example_spoken: We met the deadline with ten minutes to spare.

entries.definition: to arrive at an opinion or decision that everyone in a group accepts
entries.example_academic: Scientists have reached a consensus on the main causes of the decline.
entries.example_spoken: We couldn't reach a consensus on the topic, so we voted.

entries.definition: to remember a fact and consider it when you decide or judge something
entries.example_academic: Readers should bear in mind that the figures are estimates.
entries.example_spoken: Bear in mind that the library closes early on Fridays.

entries.definition: to make something easier to understand by providing new information
entries.example_academic: The letters shed light on the daily life of ordinary soldiers.
entries.example_spoken: Can you shed some light on why the meeting was cancelled?

entries.definition: to find a sensible middle point between two opposite needs
entries.example_academic: Planners must strike a balance between growth and conservation.
entries.example_spoken: I'm trying to strike a balance between work and sleep.

entries.definition: opinions or interests that people share even though they disagree about other things
entries.example_academic: The two schools of thought share more common ground than their supporters admit.
entries.example_spoken: We finally found some common ground on the budget.

entries.definition: to create the basic conditions that make a later development possible
entries.example_academic: These early experiments laid the foundation for modern genetics.
entries.example_spoken: The first-year courses lay the foundation for everything that follows.

entries.definition: a large amount of information that together supports a conclusion
entries.example_academic: A substantial body of evidence links exercise to improved memory.
entries.example_spoken: There's a whole body of evidence showing that cramming doesn't work.

entries.definition: to show that two things are similar in some way
entries.example_academic: The author draws a parallel between the two revolutions.
entries.example_spoken: You could draw a parallel between learning a language and learning music.

entries.definition: to reduce or remove the difference between two groups or things
entries.example_academic: The program aims to bridge the gap between school and university.
entries.example_spoken: Summer classes helped me bridge the gap in math.

entries.definition: to make people doubt whether something is true or right
entries.example_academic: The new measurements call into question the accepted age of the site.
entries.example_spoken: That mistake calls the whole report into question.

entries.definition: in a way that harms or reduces something else
entries.example_academic: Output rose at the expense of product quality.
entries.example_spoken: He got good grades at the expense of his health.

entries.definition: after considering a particular fact or new piece of information
entries.translation_fr: compte tenu de, à la lumière de
entries.example_academic: In light of these findings, the earlier model must be revised.
entries.example_spoken: In light of the weather, we're moving the event indoors.

entries.definition: to come to understand something more deeply
entries.translation_fr: mieux comprendre, avoir un aperçu de
entries.example_academic: Interviews allowed the researchers to gain insight into the workers' motives.
entries.example_spoken: The internship helped me gain insight into how a newsroom works.

entries.definition: believed or approved by most people
entries.example_academic: It is widely accepted that early diagnosis improves outcomes.
entries.example_spoken: It's widely accepted that you learn more by teaching others.

entries.definition: a question about which people still disagree
entries.example_academic: The exact date of the migration remains a matter of debate.
entries.example_spoken: Whether attendance should count is still a matter of debate.

entries.definition: facts that are strong enough to make people believe something
entries.example_academic: The trial produced compelling evidence that the drug reduces mortality.
entries.example_spoken: There's no compelling evidence that the shortcut is faster.

entries.definition: results that affect many people or things over a long time
entries.example_academic: The decision had far-reaching consequences for trade across the region.
entries.example_spoken: Dropping that course could have far-reaching consequences for your degree.

entries.definition: a part that is more important than any other in making something happen
entries.example_academic: Merchants played a pivotal role in the spread of the new religion.
entries.example_spoken: Our team captain had a pivotal role in winning the final.

entries.definition: to use power or authority to affect what happens
entries.example_academic: Large landowners exerted influence over local courts.
entries.example_spoken: Older students exert a lot of influence on the first-years.

entries.definition: unable to be true or to exist at the same time
entries.example_academic: The two explanations are not mutually exclusive and may both apply.
entries.example_spoken: Having fun and getting good grades aren't mutually exclusive.

entries.definition: information based on personal stories rather than on careful study
entries.example_academic: The claim rests on anecdotal evidence rather than controlled trials.
entries.example_spoken: That's just anecdotal evidence; your cousin isn't a study.

entries.definition: a strong personal reason for wanting something to happen, because you will gain from it
entries.example_academic: Producers have a vested interest in keeping the tariff in place.
entries.example_spoken: He has a vested interest in the club getting more money.

entries.definition: to be the opposite of something or to conflict with it
entries.example_academic: These results run counter to the predictions of the standard model.
entries.example_spoken: That idea runs counter to everything our professor said.

entries.definition: to make an idea or theory seem more likely to be true
entries.example_academic: The discovery lends support to the theory that the island was settled from the east.
entries.example_spoken: Your story lends support to what I was saying.

entries.definition: a statement about a whole group that is too broad and ignores important differences
entries.example_academic: The article relies on sweeping generalizations about an entire generation.
entries.example_spoken: That's a sweeping generalization; not all engineers hate writing.

entries.definition: to make something seem less certain or less likely to be true
entries.example_academic: Errors in the sampling cast doubt on the study's conclusions.
entries.example_spoken: The missing pages cast doubt on his whole story.

entries.definition: to remain correct or valid in a particular situation
entries.example_academic: The rule holds true for most mammals but not for bats.
entries.example_spoken: Does that still hold true if you study part-time?

entries.definition: to provide something that was missing
entries.example_academic: The study fills a gap in our knowledge of rural diets.
entries.example_spoken: This workshop fills a gap for students who never learned to cite.

entries.definition: the largest part of something
entries.example_academic: The bulk of the funding came from private donors.
entries.example_spoken: I spent the bulk of the weekend in the library.

entries.definition: the most basic reason why a problem exists
entries.example_academic: The report identifies poor drainage as the root cause of the flooding.
entries.example_spoken: The root cause of our delays is that nobody answers emails.

entries.definition: easy to get or obtain
entries.example_academic: Coal was readily available and cheaper than imported oil.
entries.example_spoken: The slides are readily available on the course page.

entries.definition: a connection in which one thing makes another happen
entries.example_academic: A correlation between two variables does not prove a causal relationship.
entries.example_spoken: There might be a link, but is it a causal relationship?

entries.definition: a very clear and noticeable difference
entries.example_academic: The wealth of the capital stood in stark contrast to the poverty of the provinces.
entries.example_spoken: Her calm was in stark contrast to everyone else's panic.

entries.definition: the view that most people accept as true without questioning it
entries.example_academic: The study challenges the conventional wisdom that breakfast improves concentration.
entries.example_spoken: Conventional wisdom says you shouldn't change your first answer.

entries.definition: results of an action that were not planned or expected
entries.example_academic: Price controls often have unintended consequences, such as shortages.
entries.example_spoken: Banning laptops in class had some unintended consequences.

entries.definition: connected so closely that the two things cannot be separated
entries.example_academic: Language and identity are inextricably linked in the history of the region.
entries.example_spoken: For me, coffee and studying are inextricably linked.

entries.definition: to make an idea seem more believable, or to accept it as possibly true
entries.example_academic: The newly discovered letters give credence to the claim that the treaty was forged.
entries.example_spoken: I wouldn't give credence to rumors about the exam.

entries.definition: a question that is no longer worth discussing because it cannot be settled or no longer matters
entries.example_academic: Whether the bridge could have been saved is now a moot point.
entries.example_spoken: It's a moot point now; the class is already full.

entries.definition: to make people want to ask an obvious question; in logic, to assume what you are trying to prove
entries.translation_fr: soulever la question ; faire une pétition de principe
entries.example_academic: The proposal begs the question of who will pay for the maintenance.
entries.example_spoken: That begs the question: why didn't anyone tell us earlier?

entries.definition: a result that is certain before it happens
entries.example_academic: With the opposition divided, the outcome of the vote was a foregone conclusion.
entries.example_spoken: Her winning the prize was a foregone conclusion.

entries.definition: to be suitable for a particular use or treatment
entries.example_academic: The material lends itself to large-scale industrial production.
entries.example_spoken: This topic lends itself to a group presentation.

entries.definition: the most important and difficult part of a problem or argument
entries.example_academic: The crux of the matter is whether the two samples are truly comparable.
entries.example_spoken: The crux of the matter is that we started too late.

entries.definition: full of problems
entries.example_academic: Any attempt to date the manuscript precisely is fraught with difficulty.
entries.example_spoken: Organizing a trip for forty people is fraught with difficulty.

entries.definition: a clear and noticeable change from what was done or expected before
entries.example_academic: The policy represented a marked departure from decades of protectionism.
entries.example_spoken: Her second essay was a marked departure from her usual style.

entries.definition: an understanding that is accepted by everyone without being put into words
entries.example_academic: There was a tacit agreement among producers not to lower prices.
entries.example_spoken: We have a tacit agreement that whoever cooks doesn't wash up.
